One lens's contribution to a resolution

Source: R/policy.R
lens_contribution.Rd

Builds the single row a lens adds to a contributions table: which lens it is, whether its estimate is grounded, whether it declined, the action it stands behind, and the reason and grounding token it declared. The row is the whole of what quorum_resolve() reads, so a lens that has abstained cannot smuggle a number into a resolution.

Usage

lens_contribution(
  lens,
  grounded,
  abstained,
  action = NA_real_,
  reason = NA_character_,
  grounding = NA_character_,
  decisive = !abstained
)

Arguments

lens

Single string naming the lens.

grounded

Single logical: is the lens's estimate grounded?

abstained

Single logical: did the lens decline to stand behind a number?

action

The action the lens stands behind, as a single number, or NA_real_ when it offers none.

reason

Single string naming why the lens declined, or NA_character_.

grounding

The grounding token the lens declared, conventionally one of orchestraManifest::GROUNDING_GROUNDED or its unverified complement, or NA_character_.

decisive

Single logical: is this lens's answer usable as the carried answer? Defaults to !abstained.

Value

A one-row data frame with the seven columns named above.

Details

decisive defaults to the complement of abstained and is separate from it because the two can come apart: a lens may fit, decline to abstain, and still have no action to offer, and a caller that knows this records decisive = FALSE rather than overloading the abstention flag.

See also

contributions() to bind rows into a table, quorum_resolve() to resolve one.

Examples

lens_contribution("mechanism", grounded = TRUE, abstained = FALSE,
                  action = 120, grounding = "grounded")
#>        lens grounded abstained action reason grounding decisive
#> 1 mechanism     TRUE     FALSE    120   <NA>  grounded     TRUE
